label: Acts 12:1
text: Now about that time, King Herod stretched out his hands to oppress some of the assembly.

label: Acts 12:2
text: He killed James, the brother of John, with the sword.

label: Acts 12:3
text: When he saw that it pleased the Jews, he proceeded to seize Peter also. This was during the days of unleavened bread.

label: Acts 12:4
text: When he had arrested him, he put him in prison, and delivered him to four squads of four soldiers each to guard him, intending to bring him out to the people after the Passover.

label: Acts 12:5
text: Peter therefore was kept in the prison, but constant prayer was made by the assembly to God for him.

label: Acts 12:6
text: The same night when Herod was about to bring him out, Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, bound with two chains. Guards in front of the door kept the prison.

label: Acts 12:7
text: And behold, an angel of the Lord stood by him, and a light shone in the cell. He struck Peter on the side, and woke him up, saying, “Stand up quickly!” His chains fell off from his hands.

label: Acts 12:8
text: The angel said to him, “Get dressed and put on your sandals.” He did so. He said to him, “Put on your cloak, and follow me.”

label: Acts 12:9
text: And he went out and followed him. He didn’t know that what was being done by the angel was real, but thought he saw a vision.

label: Acts 12:10
text: When they were past the first and the second guard, they came to the iron gate that leads into the city, which opened to them by itself. They went out, and went down one street, and immediately the angel departed from him.

label: Acts 12:11
text: When Peter had come to himself, he said, “Now I truly know that the Lord has sent out his angel and delivered me out of the hand of Herod, and from everything the Jewish people were expecting.”

label: Acts 12:12
text: Thinking about that, he came to the house of Mary, the mother of John who was called Mark, where many were gathered together and were praying.

label: Acts 12:13
text: When Peter knocked at the door of the gate, a maid named Rhoda came to answer.

label: Acts 12:14
text: When she recognized Peter’s voice, she didn’t open the gate for joy, but ran in, and reported that Peter was standing in front of the gate.

label: Acts 12:15
text: They said to her, “You are crazy!” But she insisted that it was so. They said, “It is his angel.”

label: Acts 12:16
text: But Peter continued knocking. When they had opened, they saw him, and were amazed.

label: Acts 12:17
text: But he, beckoning to them with his hand to be silent, declared to them how the Lord had brought him out of the prison. He said, “Tell these things to James, and to the brothers.” Then he departed, and went to another place.

label: Acts 12:18
text: Now as soon as it was day, there was no small stir among the soldiers about what had become of Peter.

label: Acts 12:19
text: When Herod had sought for him, and didn’t find him, he examined the guards, and commanded that they should be put to death. He went down from Judea to Caesarea, and stayed there.

label: Acts 12:20
text: Now Herod was very angry with the people of Tyre and Sidon. They came with one accord to him, and, having made Blastus, the king’s personal aide, their friend, they asked for peace, because their country depended on the king’s country for food.

label: Acts 12:21
text: On an appointed day, Herod dressed himself in royal clothing, sat on the throne, and gave a speech to them.

label: Acts 12:22
text: The people shouted, “The voice of a god, and not of a man!”

label: Acts 12:23
text: Immediately an angel of the Lord struck him, because he didn’t give God the glory, and he was eaten by worms and died.

label: Acts 12:24
text: But the word of God grew and multiplied.

label: Acts 12:25
text: Barnabas and Saul returned to Jerusalem, when they had fulfilled their service, also taking with them John who was called Mark.

variants.reading: εις Ιερουσαλημ ('to Jerusalem', the WEB wording)
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Acts of the Apostles' lists Acts 12:25 εις Ιερουσαλημ ('to Jerusalem') for א, B, H, L, P, 049, 056, 0142 and others - the reading both graph codices carry. Against it, εξ Ιερουσαλημ ('from Jerusalem') is listed for P74, A, 33, 69, 630, 2127, and απο Ιερουσαλημ ('from Jerusalem') for D, Ψ, 181, 436, 614, 2412 and lectionaries. The WEB prints the 'to Jerusalem' wording; 'from Jerusalem' would mean the pair set out from Jerusalem for Antioch instead.

label: Herod the king was Herod Agrippa I, king over Judea, Samaria and Idumea (41-44 CE)
statement: 'Herod the king' who oppressed the Jerusalem assembly was Herod Agrippa I, grandson of Herod the Great, king of Judea (with Samaria and Idumea) from 41 CE until his death in 44 CE.

label: Herod Agrippa I stretched out his hands to oppress some members of the Jerusalem assembly
statement: About 44 CE Herod Agrippa I began to oppress (kakosai) some of the church in Jerusalem.

label: Herod Agrippa I had James the brother of John killed with the sword
statement: Herod executed James, the son of Zebedee and brother of John, 'with the sword' (machaira) - beheading, the usual form of execution for Roman subjects of rank.
note: No source outside Acts records this execution. Josephus, Ant. 20.199-203, reports the execution of a different James - the brother of Jesus - by the high priest Ananus in 62 CE; the two are not to be conflated (see the related_to edge).

label: Peter was seized during the days of unleavened bread, with the plan to bring him out after the Passover
statement: The arrest fell during the days of unleavened bread (the Passover festival week), and Herod intended to bring Peter out to the people after the Passover (to pascha).
note: In Mark 14:12 the first day of unleavened bread is the day 'when they sacrificed the Passover'; Acts uses the same festival calendar (related_to link).

label: Peter was delivered to four squads of four soldiers to guard him (Roman custodia)
statement: Herod delivered the arrested Peter to four squads (tetradia, Latin quaterniones) of four soldiers each - sixteen men in four night watches - the Roman military custodia of an important prisoner.

label: The Jerusalem assembly prayed constantly to God for Peter while he was in prison
statement: While Peter was kept in prison, constant (ektenees) prayer was made by the church to God for him.

label: An angel of the Lord freed Peter from the prison by night
statement: On the last night an angel of the Lord woke Peter, his chains fell off, he passed the guards, and the iron gate of the prison opened to them of its own accord; the angel left him in the street.
note: Miracle claim. Searched Josephus, Tacitus, Suetonius and the rabbinic corpus; nothing external. Never graded from setting evidence.

label: An iron gate led from the prison into the city
statement: The prison had an iron gate (pylen sidieran) opening into the city street, passing which Peter and the angel reached the street before the angel departed.

label: Peter went to the house of Mary the mother of John called Mark, where many were praying
statement: Peter came to the house of Mary, mother of John surnamed Mark, in Jerusalem, where many had gathered and were praying - a house serving as a meeting place of the assembly.

label: The maid Rhoda answered the gate and recognized Peter's voice
statement: A maid named Rhoda came to answer Peter's knock at the gate, recognized his voice, and ran in with the news before opening the gate; the group called her mad, then said 'It is his angel', and were amazed when they saw him.

label: Peter said 'Tell these things to James and to the brothers' and went to another place
statement: Peter told the gathered believers to report his release to James and the brothers, then left for another place. The James named is unnamed in the verse and is identified by most commentators with James the brother of the Lord, already a leading figure in Jerusalem.

label: Herod examined the guards and commanded that they be put to death
statement: When Peter was found gone, there was a stir among the soldiers; Herod examined the guards (anetasesato tous apagegmenous) and ordered them led away to execution - the discipline for losing a prisoner from custody.

label: Herod went down from Judea to Caesarea and stayed there
statement: After the execution of the guards Herod went down from Judea to Caesarea and stayed there - Caesarea Maritima, the Herodian port city that served as the administrative capital.
note: Kind corrected from place to event in consolidation B: the statement is an event (the matrix anchors office/event/object/custom/time claims).

label: Tyre and Sidon sought peace with Herod through Blastus, the king's chamberlain
statement: Herod was very angry with the people of Tyre and Sidon; they came with one accord, won over Blastus, the king's chamberlain (ho epi tou koitonos), and asked for peace, because their country was nourished from the king's country.

label: Tyre and Sidon depended on the king's country for food
statement: Phoenicia's coastal cities were fed from the produce of the interior - 'their country depended on the king's country for food' - which gave Herod leverage over them.

label: Herod in royal apparel sat on the throne and addressed the people, who acclaimed him a god
statement: On an appointed day Herod put on royal clothing (endysamenos estheta basiliken), sat on the tribunal and made an oration to the delegates of Tyre and Sidon; the shouting people cried, 'The voice of a god, and not of a man!'

label: Herod was struck by an angel of the Lord, was eaten by worms, and died
statement: Immediately an angel of the Lord struck Herod because he did not give God the glory; he was eaten by worms (skolekobrotos) and died - at Caesarea, in 44 CE.
note: Sudden death at Caesarea after the acclaim is Josephus's report too (Ant. 19.343-350); the agent (angel vs omen) and manner (immediate worms vs five days of pain) differ - see the related_to edge.

label: Barnabas and Saul returned to Jerusalem after fulfilling their service, taking John Mark
statement: Barnabas and Saul returned from Jerusalem (or to Jerusalem; a textual variant) after completing the relief service, taking with them John, who was called Mark.
note: The direction variant eis/ex/apo Ierousalem is recorded on the passage node.

label: Herod Agrippa I (Marcus Julius Agrippa)
aka: Agrippa I; 'Herod the king' of Acts 12; grandson of Herod the Great
dates: 11 BCE - 44 CE; king of Judea, Samaria and Idumea 41-44 CE

label: John Mark
note: Attendant (hyperetes) of Barnabas and Paul on the first journey (13:5); he departed at Perga and returned to Jerusalem (13:13).

label: Wikipedia: Herod Agrippa
title: Herod Agrippa
excerpt: Agrippa I died suddenly from an “infestation of worms” in 44. In a Christian context he is traditionally identified as the king simply named Herod whose death is recounted in Acts 12 (12:20–23).

label: Wikipedia: Herodian coinage (Agrippa I)
title: Herodian coinage
excerpt: The most common prutah issued by Agrippa I shows a royal fringed umbrella-like canopy on the obverse, with the inscription 'ΑΓΡΙΠΑ BACIΛEΩC' ('King Agrippa') in Greek , while the reverse shows three ears of barley between two leaves with the year.

label: Wikisource: Josephus, Antiquities 19.346 (the silver garment)
title: The Antiquities of the Jews, Book XIX
excerpt: On the second day of which shows he put on a garment made wholly of silver, and of a contexture truly wonderful, and came into the theater early in the morning; at which time the silver of his garment being illuminated by the fresh reflection of the sun's rays upon it

label: Wikisource: Josephus, Antiquities 19.346 (the crowd cries 'a god')
title: The Antiquities of the Jews, Book XIX
excerpt: presently his flatterers cried out, one from one place, and another from another, (though not for his good,) that he was a god; and they added, "Be thou merciful to us; for although we have hitherto reverenced thee only as a man, yet shall we henceforth own thee as superior to mortal nature."

label: Wikisource: Josephus, Antiquities 19.350 (death after five days of pain)
title: The Antiquities of the Jews, Book XIX
excerpt: And when he had been quite worn out by the pain in his belly for five days, he departed this life, being in the fifty-fourth year of his age, and in the seventh year of his reign

label: Wikisource: Josephus, Antiquities 19.345 (Agrippa at Caesarea)
title: The Antiquities of the Jews, Book XIX
excerpt: he came to the city Cesarea, which was formerly called Strato's Tower; and there he exhibited shows in honor of Caesar, upon his being informed that there was a certain festival celebrated to make vows for his safety.

excerpt: When Judea became a Roman province in 6 CE, Caesarea replaced Jerusalem as its civilian and military capital and became the official residence of its governors, such as procurator Antonius Felix and prefect Pontius Pilatus.
